article.content: On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States , starting with a single model in 2027. They also announced a "long-term goal" of pushing the computer industry to create "a fully domestic supply chain." Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here - not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Microsoft. We're not aware of any company that does. But we are aware of companies that have briefly and strategically assembled computers here seemingly to appease President Donald Trump . article.aiArticle:
Defense contractor Anduril and semiconductor designer Qualcomm have revised their timeline for an upcoming domestically manufactured computer line, asserting that the hardware will satisfy strict domestic sourcing mandates right from its initial rollout. 

## Updated Compliance Claims for 2027 Rollout

According to a report by **The Verge**, published on **October 29, 2026**, Anduril now states that its upcoming **BlueChip** laptop will meet strict **"Buy American"** standards at launch, reaching a **65 percent domestic** threshold. This updated projection arrives shortly after the defense firm and its tech partner initially revealed their collaboration on Tuesday. During that original announcement, the two companies stated their intent to build laptops entirely in the United States, targeting a single model release in **2027**, alongside a broader, long-term objective to reshape the computer manufacturing industry. 

The defense technology sector has historically faced intense scrutiny over supply chain vulnerabilities, particularly regarding hardware components sourced from overseas manufacturing hubs. Readers interested in the origins of this hardware initiative can learn more about [Palmer Luckey’s Anduril getting into laptops and claiming they’ll be American-made](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/palmer-luckey-s-anduril-is-getting-into-laptops-and-claims-they-ll), as well as the broader context of [Anduril and Qualcomm launching BlueChip as a new kind of US-made laptop](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/anduril-qualcomm-launch-bluechip-a-new-kind-of-us-made-laptop). Manufacturing electronic equipment domestically remains an expensive and logistically complex endeavor for hardware developers accustomed to relying on Asian assembly plants.

## Broader Context and Industry Stakes

*Context: Government procurement regulations in the United States often mandate specific domestic content percentages for defense and public sector contracts, making supply chain localization a financial imperative for defense contractors. Meeting these federal thresholds allows companies like Anduril to bid on sensitive government agreements that prohibit foreign hardware components due to espionage and security concerns.*

*What to watch: Observers will be monitoring whether the partnership can realistically achieve the 65 percent domestic benchmark by 2027 without incurring massive production delays or price inflations that could hobble commercial viability.*

Sources: [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1021554/anduril-bluechip-65-percent-domestic-buy-american)
